metadata.name: Swiss Regulatory Compliance
metadata.description: FINMA and Swiss-specific regulatory rules for banking operations
metadata.author: External Plugin Author

rules.name: FINMA Qualified Investor Check
rules.description: Clients with assets below CHF 500,000 cannot be classified as qualified investors under FINMA rules
rules.condition: Total assets < CHF 500,000 AND investor type = QUALIFIED
rules.evaluateBody: var assets = parseFloat(data && data.totalAssets || 0); var isQualified = data && data.investorType === 'QUALIFIED'; if (isQualified && assets < 500000) { return { passed: false, message: 'FINMA: Qualified investor requires min CHF 500,000 (has ' + assets + ')', severity: 'error' }; } return { passed: true, message: 'FINMA qualified investor check passed', severity: 'info' };

rules.name: Swiss Withholding Tax
rules.description: Swiss domestic dividends are subject to 35% withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer)
rules.evaluateBody: var country = data && data.issuerCountry || ''; if (country === 'CH' && data && data.type === 'DIVIDEND') { return { passed: false, message: 'Swiss withholding tax of 35% applies to this dividend', severity: 'info' }; } return { passed: true, message: 'No Swiss withholding tax applicable', severity: 'info' };

testCases.businessDescription: Verify that only clients meeting the FINMA asset threshold can be classified as qualified investors.

steps.name: Retrieve client assets
steps.businessDescription: Load the client's total asset value from all portfolios and accounts.

steps.name: Check FINMA threshold
steps.businessDescription: Verify assets meet the CHF 500,000 minimum for qualified investor status.

steps.name: Apply classification
steps.businessDescription: Set or reject the qualified investor classification based on the check.

testCases.expectedResult: Client with sufficient assets is classified as qualified investor; client below threshold is rejected.
testCases.documentation: Tests FINMA-compliant qualified investor classification per Swiss Financial Services Act (FinSA).

testCases.businessDescription: Verify that dividends from Swiss issuers have 35% Verrechnungssteuer correctly applied.

steps.name: Identify Swiss issuer
steps.businessDescription: Determine if the dividend-paying instrument is a Swiss domestic security.

steps.name: Calculate withholding
steps.businessDescription: Apply the 35% Swiss withholding tax to the gross dividend amount.

steps.name: Verify net payment
steps.businessDescription: Confirm the net dividend credited equals 65% of the gross amount.

testCases.expectedResult: Net dividend after withholding tax equals 65% of gross dividend for Swiss securities.
testCases.documentation: Tests Swiss Verrechnungssteuer (anticipatory tax) calculation on domestic dividends.
